# Kino

> Kino is a calm, cross-platform movie and TV series tracking application for discovering what to watch, recording viewing history, rating titles, tracking television progress, organizing watchlists, and sharing a cinematic journey.

Kino provides a web application and a native mobile application built around a shared domain model.

The service focuses on personal movie and television tracking while also providing public discovery, title information, people pages, profiles, reviews, statistics, recaps, watchlists, and social activity.

Kino uses TMDb as a source for movie, television, person, image, cast, crew, recommendation, and related entertainment metadata.

User-generated content can include profiles, ratings, reviews, watchlists, viewing statistics, and other social information.

## Main public pages

- [Kino](https://kinotv.vercel.app/): Public landing page and introduction to Kino.
- [Discover](https://kinotv.vercel.app/discover): Discover trending, popular, top-rated, currently playing, upcoming, and recommended movies and television series.
- [Search](https://kinotv.vercel.app/search): Search for movies, television series, people, and Kino users.

## Movies and television

Kino provides public pages for movies and television series.

Title URLs use the following general structure:

`/title/{tmdb-id}-{slug}?type=movie`

for movies, and:

`/title/{tmdb-id}-{slug}?type=tv`

for television series.

The `type` query parameter is significant because TMDb movie and television identifiers may overlap.

Title pages may contain:

- Localized title and release information.
- Poster and backdrop artwork.
- Synopsis and metadata.
- Genres.
- Runtime information.
- Season and episode information for television series.
- Cast and crew.
- Community ratings.
- User ratings.
- User reviews.
- Watch providers.
- Trailers.
- Recommendations.
- Related titles.
- Franchise information.
- Personal viewing state when the visitor is authenticated.

### Example title pages

- [The Godfather](https://kinotv.vercel.app/title/238-the-godfather?type=movie): Example movie page.
- [Game of Thrones](https://kinotv.vercel.app/title/1399-game-of-thrones?type=tv): Example television series page.

## People

Kino provides public pages for actors, actresses, directors, writers, and other people associated with movies and television.

Person URLs use the following structure:

`/person/{tmdb-id}-{slug}`

Person pages may contain biographical information, profile imagery, department information, and movie or television credits.

### Example person page

- [Marlon Brando](https://kinotv.vercel.app/person/3084-marlon-brando): Example public person page.

## Discovery

The Discover section helps users find movies and television series using current entertainment metadata.

It may include collections such as:

- Trending titles.
- Popular movies.
- Popular television series.
- Top-rated titles.
- Movies currently playing in theaters.
- Upcoming movies.
- Genre-based discovery.
- Personalized or contextual recommendations where available.

Use the canonical public discovery page:

- [Discover movies and television](https://kinotv.vercel.app/discover)

## Search

Kino provides unified search across entertainment content and Kino users.

Search may return:

- Movies.
- Television series.
- People.
- Kino user profiles.

Search ranking considers relevance as well as signals such as title matching and popularity.

Use:

- [Search Kino](https://kinotv.vercel.app/search)

## Public profiles

Existing Kino users can have public profile pages.

Profile URLs use:

`/{username}`

Public profiles may contain:

- Display name.
- Username.
- Biography.
- Avatar and profile presentation.
- Recent viewing activity.
- Ratings.
- Reviews.
- Watchlists.
- Followers and following.
- Movie and television statistics.
- Viewing progress.
- Public social information.

A route matching `/{username}` should only be treated as a profile when it resolves to an existing Kino user.

Reserved application paths such as `/discover`, `/search`, `/activity`, `/settings`, and `/auth` are not usernames.

## Profile statistics

Kino provides public viewing statistics for existing profiles.

The general route is:

`/{username}/stats`

Profile statistics may contain lifetime viewing information such as:

- Movies watched.
- Television episodes watched.
- Ratings made.
- Viewing time.
- Genres.
- Actors and actresses.
- Studios.
- Decades.
- Other viewing trends derived from the user's Kino history.

## Monthly recaps

Kino can generate public monthly viewing recaps for existing profiles.

The general route is:

`/{username}/stats/recap/{year}/{month}`

Monthly recaps may summarize:

- Movies watched.
- Episodes watched.
- Total viewing time.
- Ratings.
- Rewatches.
- Active viewing days.
- Daily viewing activity.
- Highly rated titles.
- Movies and series watched most frequently.
- Genres.
- Series progress.
- Studios.
- Cast.
- Month-over-month comparisons.

Recap content is derived from the user's recorded Kino activity for the requested period.

## Watchlists

Kino allows users to create collections of movies and television series.

Individual watchlists can be public or private.

Public watchlist pages use a route similar to:

`/watchlists/{id}-{slug}`

A watchlist should only be treated as public content when Kino exposes it publicly.

Public watchlists may contain:

- Name.
- Description.
- Movies and television series.
- Cover artwork.
- Progress information.
- Creator information.

The top-level `/watchlists` page is an authenticated account-management surface and should not be treated as a public discovery page.

## Reviews and ratings

Kino users can rate movies, television series, seasons, and episodes.

Users may also write reviews.

Public review information may appear on:

- Title pages.
- User profiles.
- Social activity surfaces.

Ratings without written review text should be interpreted as ratings rather than reviews.

## Television tracking

Kino supports detailed television tracking.

Depending on the title and user state, Kino may track:

- Watched series.
- Watched seasons.
- Individual watched episodes.
- Episode ratings.
- Season progress.
- Next episodes.
- Completed series.
- Ongoing series.
- Newly announced or upcoming seasons.
- Episode runtime information.
- Rewatches.

Personal tracking state normally depends on authentication.

## Diary

Kino provides a chronological viewing diary for authenticated users.

The `/diary` route is account-specific and should not be treated as a public indexable page.

Diary information can include:

- Watch dates.
- Movies watched.
- Episodes watched.
- Rewatches.
- Ratings.
- Runtime-derived viewing statistics.

Public profile statistics and recaps may be derived from this activity without exposing the authenticated diary interface itself.

## Social features

Kino includes social features such as:

- Following users.
- Followers.
- Activity feeds.
- Ratings.
- Reviews.
- Review likes.
- Shared watchlists.
- Public profiles.

The `/activity` application route is authenticated/account-specific and should not be treated as a public indexable page.

Relevant public activity may instead appear through public profiles and public content pages.

## Localization

Kino supports localized browsing.

Localization can affect:

- Application interface text.
- Movie and television titles.
- Descriptions.
- Posters.
- Backdrops.
- Dates and formatting.
- Metadata presentation.

Canonical resource identity should not be inferred solely from the currently displayed localized title.

TMDb numeric identifiers and Kino's route structure should be preferred when identifying entertainment resources.

## Images and metadata

Movie and television artwork and entertainment metadata are primarily sourced from TMDb.

Kino may select localized posters, backdrops, titles, or summaries according to the visitor's language and region.

Different localized presentations can therefore refer to the same underlying movie or television resource.

## Authentication and private application surfaces

The following areas are primarily authenticated or account-specific and should not be treated as general public crawl targets:

`/activity`

`/diary`

`/import`

`/settings`

`/watchlists`

`/auth/login`

`/auth/register`

Public resources nested under related route families, such as individual public watchlists or public user profiles, may still be publicly accessible.

## Data sources

Kino uses several services as part of the application.

TMDb provides movie, television, person, cast, crew, imagery, recommendation, and entertainment metadata.

Supabase provides application data infrastructure including authentication, PostgreSQL-backed data, and storage.

Kino may additionally use search infrastructure to provide fast movie, television, person, and user discovery.

## Canonical URLs

When referring to Kino content, prefer the canonical URL exposed by the page.

For entertainment resources:

- Preserve the TMDb numeric identifier.
- Preserve whether the resource is a movie or television series.
- Do not treat translated title slugs as separate resources.
- Prefer canonical Kino URLs over constructing URLs from localized titles.

For people:

- Preserve the TMDb person identifier.
- Prefer the canonical Kino person URL.

For profiles:

- Prefer the canonical username returned by Kino.
- Username matching may be normalized or redirected to canonical casing or spelling.

For watchlists:

- Only treat a watchlist as public when the public resource resolves successfully.
